Each result's masked zone, scaled back 1:1, is the object's state image (companions-02) composited over the UNCHANGED plate with an 8 px feathered edge; the funeral sheet is placed on the new board; the plane-1 occlusion mask is an authored silhouette of the new trough. Plate file unchanged. Live proofs: Thad in front of and behind the trough, the funeral state in Act III.

PHASE 1.5E (owner review of 1.5D: the board and the trough still read as separate pieces composited over the environment): STRATEGY CHANGED -- the board's structure and the trough are PLATE. Preflight diagnosis: the two source panels were stitched at x 1704-1800 through the west panel's board, whose right half was a ghost fused into the east storefront's porch; the church was intact outside the seam (not repainted above y 335 or left of x 1585). REGION A (1 of 1): the board freestanding on two posts on the boardwalk with its ordinary papers, the church's lower right wall continued behind it, the storefront porch's left end finished, clear air between. REGION B (1 of 1): the trough and the east hitching rail authored together as one scene -- a low trough beside the rail's west end with a stride of mud between. Both zones composited INTO a new plate (street-candidate-03); the 1.5D overlays retired. posted_notices ORDINARY = the plate, FUNERAL = a sheet-only overlay on the same board; water_trough has no state image, its occlusion (and the rail's) is the room's plane-1 authored silhouette mask; mud_far and mud_mid plane 1; obstacles and the hotspot re-authored from the new geometry.

PHASE 1.5F (Tyler's review of 1.5E: strongly positive, three narrow issues): (1) THE SIGN, 0 operations -- the plate's board is level and the LETTERING was not: the type carried +1.43 deg of slant inherited from the shipping source crop (whose board was angled) and that crop's wood at partial alpha. The letters are cut on their own ramp, de-rotated to a residual of 0.05 deg and centred on the board's inner face with even margins; both states from the one corrected lettering. (2) THE CHAPEL, 1 operation, conditional and proven: with the board cloned out for diagnosis the facade had no door, no window, no step and no plinth -- not a stitch artifact, not the board's fault, so the brief's Case 2. One tightly masked repair gave it a door, a lintel, steps, two small windows and a base; the frozen notice board was composited back by its own wood-hue silhouette and the model's own painted board covered with the chapel's siding. (3) THE RAIL, 0 operations -- its obstacle was 115 px deep from y 700 and the compiler carves a band's whole column under an obstacle, so the entire band behind the rail was unwalkable and an actor could only stand on the rail's line. The obstacle is now the rail's own ground line (y 776-816, measured off the posts' feet at 786 and 812); mud_far and mud_mid are walkable ground behind it at plane 1 and mud_near is plane 0 in front, so depth follows the foot baseline for any actor -- Thad and the pie woman alike.

PHASE 1.5G (Tyler's live review of 1.5F: the art passes and is frozen; three runtime defects). 0 image operations, no pixel of the environment changed. (1) THE RAIL IS A BARRIER ON ITS OWN TWO LINES: the bar is drawn across y 640-682 and the far mud was walkable at those depths, so a click on the rail put his FEET where the bar is drawn -- a man standing on a fence. The bar's line (y 636-690) and the posts' feet (776-816) are both obstacles now, with real ground between them (mud_mid, 690-776) and in front (from 816); crossing at mid-span routes round an end. `keepsGroundAbove` is a new obstacle flag in the compiler, because carving a band used to drop everything above the obstacle and that is what left nowhere to stand behind the rail. (2) THE TROUGH'S MASK IS CUT FROM THE TROUGH: the Phase 1.5E six-point polygon was a convex hull round a box in oblique projection, swallowing a wedge of mud above the far rim and the contact shadow below the near wall -- 2995 pixels of mud that clipped a man's shins when he stood clear of the trough. The mask is now segmented from the plate's own pixels and trimmed at the trough's base line: 18800 px against 22576, and every one of them inside the object. Its obstacle sits on that base line too, so the wedge where a man stood in front of the trough and the band still called him behind it is gone. (3) THE SIGN IS REBUILT LETTER BY LETTER: rotating the whole crop levelled the block and left each letter where the old angled board put it, which is what still read as crooked. Each authored glyph is moved by whole pixels -- never rotated, never resampled -- onto its line's own row: baseline spread 6 px -> 0 and 7 px -> 0. Two new validators hold all of it: check-occluder-bounds (a mask stays inside the art it was cut from; it fails on the old polygon by 2995 px) and check-sign-baselines (letters on one row, both states the same geometry).

PHASE 1.5H (Tyler: Thad could still walk through the rail, front to back and back to front). 0 image operations. THE ROOT CAUSE, found by sampling the live walk rather than its two ends: Phase 1.5G's footing obstacle stopped at x 2270 -- the bar's own west tip -- and the trough's obstacle ended at 2236, leaving a 34 px gap between them. The router picks the crossing point NEAREST the destination, so every front-to-back walk in the rail's span crossed at x 2268: the exact tip of the bar. On screen that is a man walking through the end of the fence, and no start/end screenshot could show it. THE FIX is one continuous barrier on the fence's own ground line, x 2236 (the trough's east edge) to 2652 (40 px clear of the bar's east tip), y 776-816 -- the whole gap between the ground behind the fence (mud_mid, to 776) and the ground in front (mud_near, from 816). Both sides stay fully walkable along the whole rail; the only crossings are round the east end at x 2652, clear of the rail, or west of the trough at x 1976. The room now declares its own contract as data (`navigation.barriers`), and tools/gauntlet/rail-crossing.mjs drives the live candidate like a player -- five x positions each way, plus six clicks on the fence itself -- sampling his feet every 120 ms and asserting the side only ever changes outside the span. On the Phase 1.5G geometry that test fails all ten of ten attempts, every one of them at x 2268-2276.

PHASE 1.5I (Tyler, having manually tested 1.5H: he can still put Thad onto and through the hitching-rail geometry in the live room). 0 image operations. THE OWNER RULING retires dual-side navigation for this rail: Thad walks only on its FRONT side, round its ends where the street is open, and nowhere behind it. WHY 1.5H STILL FAILED: it answered whether he could CROSS the fence, and that was never the question. The strip behind the rail -- mud_mid_3, x 2268-2614, y 690-776 -- was legal ground, and it is exactly where the bar is drawn, so standing on it IS standing in the fence however he arrived. 1.5G's proof, 1.5H's proof and both of their tests were all consistent with the thing Tyler was seeing. Reproduced live before anything was changed: the same click test run against the complete 1.5H build fails 31 ways, and puts him behind or on the rail on nine of nine clicks -- on the bar at 2443,636, on the near post at 2305,699, on the far post at 2568,769. THE FIX is one obstacle instead of a barrier: rail_east becomes x 2236-2652, y 600-816, the whole rear of the rail's span from the top of the far mud to the top of the front band, and the compiler CARVES it -- no walk box exists behind the rail, so there is nothing for the router to find. rail_east_bar is retired with the ground it kept. A second obstacle, rail_east_post_far, carries the front ground down to 824 across x 2545-2593, because the far post's foot is 812 and the band began at 816: four pixels is not a margin. In front, mud_near is unbroken along the whole rail; past either end the street is ordinary street at every depth. THE POINTER needed a rule of its own: a click behind the rail is a click on no box, and `nearest` would have answered with the BOARDWALK, which is closer in pixels and on the far side of the fence -- so the room declares `navigation.frontOnly` and WalkBoxes.target() restricts a DESTINATION inside that region to boxes at or below y 816. `nearest` itself is untouched, which is why a figure standing behind the rail is still drawn behind it. CONSEQUENCES, both forced and both taken: the saloon's own approach point and arrival move up onto the boardwalk (y 610 and 620 -> 592, x untouched), because its door is dead centre of the rail's span and every point in the mud in front of it was behind the rail; and the pie woman, who stands behind the rail, now declares her plane on her placement, as Room 5's Winnie does behind her counter -- her position and art are untouched and her approach radius is MARKED FOR PHASE 2 RESTAGING. The two rear-side occlusion proof points are deleted with their ground; the plane-1 mask is deliberately NOT re-cut, because one file masks both the rail and the frozen trough. Proved live by tools/gauntlet/rail-front-only.mjs -- eighteen clicks, feet sampled every 120 ms -- and as geometry by tests/front-only-rail.test.ts, which asserts no walk box lies behind the rail at all.
